Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: sleight of hand — the foundational craft of close-up and parlor magic, named in English from the 14th century. Counter to Houdin & Co. (spelling-collision with Houdini trademark) and Pepper Effect (more useful in Creative).
Modern.industrySummary: Modern magic brands compete on craft literacy and editorial framing — close-up magicians, prop makers, and magic-theory publishers serving a literate enthusiast market.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Theory11 (theory11.com) plays the modern editorial peer. Ellusionist (ellusionist.com) holds the digital-magic middle. Vanishing Inc. (vanishingincmagic.com) is the editorial reference. We sit as a craft-led modern brand.
Modern.positioningStatement: Sleight Studio is a modern magic brand publishing close-up magic decks, props, and craft books.

targetAudience.primary: Close-up magicians and enthusiasts 22-45 who care about technique.

dos: Name the sleight and the inventor

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: SLEIGHT STUDIO set in a confident modern grotesk, two lines. Small mark: a single playing-card silhouette used on decks.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: A modern grotesk plus its mono — the craft-notebook register.

Luxury.tagline: Parisian conjuring, in the atelier tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Jean-Eugène Robert-Houdin (1805-1871), the French watchmaker who founded modern theatrical magic at his Théâtre Robert-Houdin in Paris in 1845. He died in 1871, deep public domain. Counter to The Circle (Magic Circle is an active London society) and Davenport Heritage (Davenports London is an active business).
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury magic is a small editorial category — heritage prop-making, atelier-grade illusions, and concierge magic for private theaters and collectors.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Tannen's Magic (tannens.com) plays the heritage New York peer. Penguin Magic (penguinmagic.com) holds the institutional middle. Theory11 (theory11.com) is the modern editorial reference. We sit as a Parisian atelier heritage house.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Maison Robert-Houdin is a heritage Parisian magic atelier drawing on Robert-Houdin's 1845 theatrical tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Magic collectors and private-theater patrons commissioning bespoke illusions.

dos: Name the illusion and the year
Send a paper card with each commission

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: MAISON ROBERT-HOUDIN set in a refined French book serif, two lines centered. A small mark — a single 19th-century stage-curtain silhouette — used as the seal.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for body and commission letters
typography.rationale: Two classical serifs — the Parisian-atelier letter register.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: sleight of hand — the foundational craft of magic, named in English from the 14th century. Single word, no TM risk. Counter to Ghost (Pepper's Ghost is reused in Creative) and Houdin (Houdini-spelling collision).
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimalist magic brands serve the craft-literate market — single-deck publishers, single-prop makers, and editorial publications that strip the lifestyle scaffolding.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most magic brands lean ornate-theatrical. The minimal end is mostly empty. Theory11 (theory11.com) is the closest editorial reference. We sit as the single-word minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Sleight is a minimal magic brand publishing one deck and one craft book.

targetAudience.primary: Close-up magicians 22-45 who buy fewer, considered tools.

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: SLEIGHT set very large in a clean modern sans, seven letters, one word. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for technique notes
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the single-craft register.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the historic division of magic between stage illusion (grand cabinets, levitations) and salon/close-up magic (cards, coins) — the two recognized branches of the trade. Counter to Magic Circle Holdings (active society) and Robert-Houdin Group (overlap with luxury pick).
Corporate.industrySummary: B2B magic operators — prop-makers serving stage productions, event-magic agencies, and salon-magic publishers — are a real institutional category serving cruise lines, casinos, and corporate events.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: The Illusionists tour (theillusionists.com) plays the stage-production reference. Magic Castle (magiccastle.com) holds the salon-magic institutional. Penguin Magic (penguinmagic.com) is the publisher reference. We sit as a B2B stage-and-salon operator.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Stage & Salon Co. is an institutional magic operator providing props, talent, and salon-magic publishing for productions and venues.

targetAudience.primary: Producers, casino entertainment buyers, and corporate event planners booking magic talent.

dos: Lead with the talent roster and the prop catalog
donts: No social media at the parent level

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: STAGE & SALON CO. set in an institutional serif, two lines. A small mark — a stage-curtain and parlor-table silhouette — used on contracts.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the booking-agent register.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Pepper's Ghost — the theatrical illusion first publicly demonstrated by John Henry Pepper at the Royal Polytechnic Institution in 1862, which projected ghostly figures onto a stage using angled glass. The technique is in the public domain and the name is editorially perfect.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative magic brands play on theatrical narrative and illusion history. Pepper's Ghost as a brand frame is editorially rich and almost unused commercially.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Theory11 (theory11.com) plays the editorial-modern peer. Vanishing Inc. (vanishingincmagic.com) holds the editorial-craft middle. The Conjuring Arts Research Center (conjuringarts.org) is the heritage reference. We sit as a 19th-century-theatrical creative brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: Pepper's Ghost is a creative magic brand drawing on 19th-century Victorian stage illusion.

targetAudience.primary: Magicians and theatrical enthusiasts 25-50 who read illusion history.

dos: Name the illusion and the inventor

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: PEPPER'S GHOST set in a Victorian display serif, two lines centered. A small mark — a single angled-glass-and-figure silhouette — used as the seal.

typography.primary: Caslon Antique for the wordmark and headlines
typography.rationale: A Victorian display serif plus a clean grotesk — the 1862-program register, modernized.
